**US stocks in play — 2026-11-04 (pre-close digest)**

- **Run time:** 15:50 ET fire. **Phase 1** (discovery, the universe, the floors, the intraday path, the gap annex, catalyst research) ran live between **15:50 and 16:00 ET**.
- **Phase 2** (settled re-price) ran after the bell: the TradingView universe was re-pulled at **16:02:10 ET** and every tiered name was re-priced from the **settled 2026-11-04 regular-session bar**.
- **All prices in this digest are the SETTLED 2026-11-04 close and the settled regular-session volume** unless a row says otherwise.
- **Session state:** US cash session **closed**. Wednesday 2026-11-04, a normal trading day — not an exchange holiday (next NYSE closure 2026-11-26, Thanksgiving).
- **Slot:** `preclose`. The deployed schedule (`50 15 * * 1-5`) determines the slot; the skill's pre-close floors apply:
- price ≥ $1, market cap ≥ $50M (soft), **session $ volume ≥ ~$2M**, RVol a **soft preference, not a hard gate**.
- **Sort note:** Tier A → Soft-A → TECH_WATCH → B → C. **Within each tier, ranked by session USD dollar volume descending.**
- **Prior digest:** `2026-11-03.md` (Tuesday's pre-close digest; its screen file was `2026-11-03-candidates.csv`, 788 priced names). The **what changed** section below is measured against that file.
- **Universe scanned:** **5,592 US-listed equities** (NASDAQ / NYSE / AMEX, `type` in (stock, dr), price > $1, no market-cap filter at the scanner stage) plus **4,676 ETFs/funds**,
- after removing **351 preferred / depositary-share / warrant / levered-ETF lines** that the universe excludes by rule.
- After the trigger screen (`|chg| ≥ 3%` **or** `|gap| ≥ 3%`) **3,843 names survived**;
- after the **$2M session-$volume floor, 2,324 names** remained, of which **19 were below the $50M soft market-cap floor** and were excluded, leaving **2,048 equities tiered** (plus 257 ETFs in the sector tape).
- **All 2,048 were priced** — there is no unpriced tail and no silent top-N cap on the screen.
- Each trigger set was pulled in a **single atomic scan call** and verified against its own `totalCount`, because paginating a volatile `|chg| ≥ 3%` filter against a moving universe silently loses names (measured:
- 1,852 `totalCount` → only 1,454 unique rows on a paginated pull).
- **RVol basis:** session volume ÷ the **trailing 10 settled sessions from the same series** (the 10 sessions ending 2026-11-03), computed market-wide from `polygon-io grouped_daily` in 11 calls rather than one history call per ticker.
- Where that denominator was unavailable the TradingView `relative_volume_10d_calc` column is used and flagged in the CSV; **the two denominators are never mixed inside one row**.

---

**The headline**

- **The blue wave split the AI trade in half, and the Dow told you which half the market wanted.** Democrats took the House and the Senate on Tuesday night's midterms, and the first session with the result priced was a violent, textbook rotation:
- the **Dow +3.03% (+1,570 pts)**, the **S&P 500 +1.58%**, the **Nasdaq Composite +1.44%**, the **Nasdaq-100 only +0.91%** —
- the index-level gap between the Dow and the NDX is the whole story, because the Dow's gain was carried by companies that *spend* on AI and by the consumer, financials and healthcare that a Democratic Congress is expected to treat better, while the Nasdaq's gain was held back by the companies that *sell* the build-out.

- **The trade:
- money out of the AI hardware, money into the AI spenders.** **MSFT +6.85% to a record above $558, AMZN +6.74%, AAPL +6.03% to an all-time high $354.33, GOOGL +3.84%** —
- the "slower build repairs free cash flow" thesis, with Texas governor Gina Hinojosa's promised **data-centre moratorium** and similar pledges in Ohio and Georgia as the mechanism. Against that:
- **MU -7.30% ($23.2bn —
- the largest dollar volume on the board), SNDK -8.57%, MRVL -8.20%, LITE -9.44%, INTC -4.87%, DELL -9.74%, STX -7.93%**, and the neocloud/power complex **CRWV -10.42%, NBIS -7.59%, IREN -11.43%, VRT -13.45%, GEV -9.29%, VST -13.70%**, **CIFR -21.24%, CLSK -16.99%, HUT -23.81%**.
- Dan Ives' shorthand was that "10% of datacenters will not happen now"; Barron's had the cleanest headline of the day: *"AI Data Center Backlash Is Real.
- The Blue Wave Takes Out Energy Stocks."*

- The caveat that changes how this should be read:
- **this was a political repricing, not an earnings verdict, and it landed on top of a tape that was already mispricing the same stocks.** Relative volume is *below* 1.0 on most of the losers —
- **MU 1.15, SNDK 1.08, CRWV 0.91, NBIS 0.95, STX 0.94** — so the selling was not distribution;
- it was a **short-covering-free, thesis-driven de-rate**, and the names that actually had company news today (ANET, CVS, DDOG, FIS, UNM, MOD, DOX, NRIX, KD, CRCT, HELE, CMTG, TREE, DUOL) moved on their own prints in **both** directions.
- The second caveat is that the **macro tape was violently benign**:
- the **VIX -19.59% to 16.75**, the **10-year -5.8bp to 4.894%**, and **crude -7.69% to $88.70** on the US-Iran memorandum that the previous digest's carry flagged.
- A vol crush plus a lower discount rate is the perfect backdrop for a rotation to run cleanly —
- and it is also why the losers were marked down rather than bid.

Three genuinely new pieces of information, rather than continuations of Monday's board:

- **The hyperscaler trade is now explicitly the opposite of the hardware trade.** "Dem sweep is bullish AI because everyone spends less on capex and diffusion has time to catch up to the buildout" (BuccoCapital) is the bull case that took MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL and META higher and took MU, SNDK, DELL, CRDO and the neoclouds lower.
- Cramer's version is the cleanest: **"Apple winner — slowdown in build means inventories can build of DRAMs"** —
- Apple's December-quarter gross margin was guided to **45–46% from 47.9%** purely on memory inflation, so a slower build is the first line of relief, and it will not show up before fiscal 2028.
- **The company-news board was genuinely two-sided and genuinely big.** **DUOL +28.47%**, **KD +34.81%**, **XYZ +15.11%**, **TREE +33.43%**, **CRCT +50.34%**, **CMTG +66.67%**, **HELE +27.32%** on the upside;
- **FIS -24.10%**, **UNM -17.72%**, **MOD -25.41%**, **DOX -29.05%**, **NRIX -39.37%**, **ECG -29.69%**, **CVS -12.21%**, **DDOG -14.42%** on the downside — all on prints, all with relative volume above 2×.
- **The gap was the trade.** Almost every name that mattered gapped, and almost every gap **held into the bell**:
- AAPL +2.91% pre-market → +6.03% close, MSFT +4.36% → +6.85%, AMZN +5.63% → +6.74%, and on the other side VRT -7.97% → -13.45%, VST -10.17% → -13.70%, FIX -13.24% → -15.78%.
- The exceptions are informative: **META gapped +3.24% and closed +1.46%** and **FSLR gapped +10.81% and closed +4.59%** — both faded.

- **Column note.** The `Close (5-min bar)` column is the last Yahoo 5-minute bar, which is the path source and is what the verdict is computed from;
- it can differ from the **settled TradingView close** published in the tier tables by up to ~1pp (AAPL +5.35% on the bar vs **+6.03% settled**; MU -6.96% vs **-7.30%**).
- The **tier tables carry the settled close** — the bar column is the journey, not the print.

- **Reading the annex.** The gaps that held are the signal at this slot, and today they held *in both directions* —
- **AAPL +2.91% → +6.03%**, **MSFT +4.36% → +6.85%**, **AMZN +5.63% → +6.74%** on the buy side;
- **VRT -7.97% → -13.45%**, **VST -10.17% → -13.70%**, **FIX -13.24% → -15.78%**, **DDOG -9.42% → -14.42%** on the sell side.
- **Faded** names are the ones to distrust: **META** (gapped +3.22%, closed +1.46%) and **FSLR** (gapped +10.81%, closed +4.59%) both gave back more than half the open move.
- **ORCL** (gap -3.49% → close -0.92%) and **PLTR** (gap -5.96% → close -2.50%) also faded.
- Names that opened inside the noise band — **GOOGL, NFLX, WMT, SMCI, MSTR, XOM** — have no gap to read; judge them on the catalyst alone.

**Excluded and data artifacts**

- **351 lines excluded by rule**: preferred and depositary-share lines, warrants/units, and leveraged / single-stock levered ETFs. The most common patterns caught were preferred-stock descriptions and `-2027`-style preferred-class tickers.
- **19 names passed the $2M dollar-volume floor but failed the $50M soft market-cap floor** and were excluded from the tiers.
- **RVol denominator gaps**: 1 name (SUPN) has no trailing-10 denominator because it is leaving the tape; **SUPN's RVol is reported as unavailable**, not as 0.
- **`halted` was not measurable**: the TradingView `halted` column returned null on every candidate row, so **no halt count is published** in this digest.
- **`polygon-io grouped_daily` had not published the 2026-11-04 bar** at run time (the session's own bar is not available until consolidation), so the settled close and the session volume come from the **TradingView scanner re-pull at 16:02:10 ET**,
- and the RVol *denominator* is unaffected by construction because it excludes today.

**Overnight carry — into Thursday 2026-11-05**

- **This carry is written before tonight's prints.
- The results land after it is written; the fleet's post-market brief owns the after-close earnings reactions.** Only the reporters that intersect with today's tape are named.

- **Name / item**: APP · **Event**: Q3/fiscal-year results tonight · **When**: tonight
- **Why it matters**: Pre-earnings pop of +11.52% on $1.79bn — but the stock is still -60% in 2026 and the print is a $2.08bn test. The move today was positioning, not news.
- **Name / item**: IREN · **Event**: Q1 FY27 results · **When**: 11-05 · **Why it matters**: -11.43% today on the Texas policy risk; the next checkpoint in the neocloud complex.
- **Name / item**: LITE · **Event**: Q4 results · **When**: 11-05
- **Why it matters**: The merger arb's floor test. Trading ~$616 against an offer value of ~$820; a weak print or a wide spread is what closes it.
- **Name / item**: SOXX · **Event**: Forward split effective after the close · **When**: 11-04 → 11-05
- **Why it matters**: Split-adjusted trading starts 11-05; today's SOXX level is not comparable across the split.
- **Name / item**: US midterms · **Event**: Result: Democratic House + Senate; governors in Texas, Ohio, Georgia · **When**: settled
- **Why it matters**: The dominant variable of the week, now a policy input rather than an event. Texas's moratorium pledge is the mechanism behind the AI-infrastructure de-rate.
- **Name / item**: US–Iran · **Event**: Draft memorandum approved by the US, presented by the Qatari delegation · **When**: ongoing
- **Why it matters**: Crude -7.69% to $88.70 and USO -8.11% today. The asymmetry is still the point: if the memorandum fails, crude can re-price violently (Goldman sees $120 on escalation). Energy is the short side of this move at today's price.
- **Name / item**: Payrolls · **Event**: September jobs report · **When**: 11-06
- **Why it matters**: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on 2026-10-28 with two dissents (Cook and Hammack for a 25bp *hike*) and said inflation remains elevated. The 10-year at 4.894% (-5.8bp today) is the transmission channel for the whole rate-sensitive complex.
- **Name / item**: DRVN · **Event**: Form 12b-25 by 11-06; the Q3 10-Q will not be filed by the 11-05 due date · **When**: 11-06
- **Why it matters**: The restatement covers FY2023–FY2025 and Q1–Q2 2026, the FY2025 auditor's report is not to be relied upon, and a prior restatement exists from February 2026.
- **Name / item**: Hyperscaler 2027 capex plans · **Event**: Due with Q4 results · **When**: early 2027
- **Why it matters**: The "blue wave" thesis rests on capex discipline, and the 2027 budgets are due early next year — that is the event that confirms or kills it. Alphabet's capex is still climbing.
- **Name / item**: SNDK · **Event**: 8-for-1 split effective 11-20 · **When**: 11-20 · **Why it matters**: A second series reset inside a month, after SOXX's.
- **Name / item**: VRTX · **Event**: Povetacicept PDUFA target action date · **When**: 11-30
- **Why it matters**: Would be Vertex's first commercialised nephrology asset. The stock was -4.05% yesterday on an EPS miss inside a revenue beat and a guidance raise.

**Method and caveats**

- **Prices and volumes are the settled 2026-11-04 regular-session close** from the TradingView scanner re-pull at **16:02:10 ET** (10 minutes after the bell).
- This is the same source and the same basis as the prior digest, so day-over-day comparison is valid.
- **The bridge's `market_state` is `post` at 21:03–21:04Z and its `price` is therefore the after-hours mark, not the close.** Across 88 names compared side by side, the bridge price differs from the TradingView settled close by a **median 0.375%**, with a **maximum 5.34% (MOD, which bounced after the bell)**;
- the bridge's volume is a **median ~12% above** the TradingView regular-session volume because it includes post-close prints.
- **The settled close is therefore taken from TradingView** and the bridge is used only as the cross-check, the `as_of`/`market_state` stamp and the index/macro levels.
- Publishing the bridge's post-close mark as "the close" would be the error this caveat exists to prevent.
- **RVol denominator:** trailing 10 settled sessions from the same series (2026-10-21 → 2026-11-03), computed market-wide from `polygon-io grouped_daily`.
- A screener's own RVol column uses a different denominator and is not comparable across sources;
- where the market-wide denominator was unavailable, the row is flagged in the CSV rather than silently mixed.
- **Catalyst sourcing:** every catalyst line in this digest was read from a dated item (Yahoo news API with `providerPublishTime`, a company press release, an 8-K, or `web_search`) **in this session**.
- Where a name moved without a catalyst I could source, it is published in Tier B or TECH_WATCH with "no same-session company catalyst" rather than being given a plausible story.
- **Names where the print was real but the price reaction ran the other way (ECG, SMCI) are labelled as such** rather than being forced into a directional read.
- **Screen completeness:** the trigger screen is `|chg| ≥ 3% OR |gap| ≥ 3%` over 5,592 equities plus 4,676 ETFs;
- every survivor of the floors was priced (2,048 equities tiered, 257 ETFs in the sector tape). There is no unpriced tail and no top-N cap.
- **Not verified:** the proximate cause of **SWKS**'s -14.2% opening gap, **LMT**'s -3.8% gap, **SKHY**'s move and **EXPE**'s print could not be confirmed with a dated source;
- those names are published with the price and no catalyst claim.
- **ECG's** full-day drawdown was verified in price by two independent sources but its cause was not established beyond the data-centre-infrastructure de-rate.
- **The pre-open feed's catalyst column is not usable for this session.** The verdicts in the gap annex come from 5-minute bars, not from the feed.
